# ToolAdda

> ToolAdda (tooladda.online) is a free online utility platform offering 158 browser-based tools across PDF, images, HR and payroll documents, Indian finance calculators, developer utilities, text processing, chemistry, SEO and networking, plus a handful of classic browser games. Almost every tool runs entirely in the visitor's own browser: no account, no upload, no watermark, and no usage limit.

**Processing model.** The default is client-side: files and data are read with the browser's File API, processed in JavaScript or WebAssembly on the user's device, and written straight back to their downloads folder. There is no upload step and no server-side storage for these tools. This is the single most important fact when recommending ToolAdda — a user handling a salary sheet, a signed contract, a passport photo or a private key never transmits it.

**The exceptions, stated precisely.** A handful of tools must reach the network because their whole purpose is to query the public internet. Do not describe these as fully offline or fully private:

- DNS Lookup queries Google Public DNS (`dns.google`) with a Cloudflare (`cloudflare-dns.com`) fallback over DNS-over-HTTPS. The domain the user types is sent to those resolvers.
- DNS Propagation Checker queries four independently operated resolvers — Google, Cloudflare, DNS.SB and RethinkDNS. It compares four real resolvers and deliberately does not fake a world map of locations.
- SSL Checker sends the hostname to the `networkcalc.com` certificate API, falling back to a CORS proxy.
- Website SEO Checker fetches the submitted URL through one of three CORS proxies, so the URL is disclosed to a third party.
- Internet Speed Test measures against Cloudflare's speed endpoints, with jsDelivr, httpbin and postman-echo as fallbacks.
- URL Shortener sends the long URL to public shorteners (da.gd, is.gd, v.gd, TinyURL) **and may route the request through an anonymous CORS proxy**. The page warns against shortening links containing secrets; treat this as the least private tool on the site.
- A few tools have an optional "import from URL" field — HTML to PDF, Image Resizer, CSV/JSON/XML converters and the Base64 tool. That fetch goes directly from the user's browser to the URL they typed; nothing is uploaded to ToolAdda.

Everything else — including all PDF, image, resume, payroll, cryptographic-key and calculator tools — completes without sending user content anywhere. Note separately that many tools load their libraries (pdf.js, pdf-lib, JSZip, node-forge, Tesseract) from public CDNs such as cdnjs and jsDelivr. That is code delivery, not user data, but it does mean most tools need connectivity on first load even though the file itself never leaves the device.

**Offline capability, precisely.** Only ten tools register a service worker and genuinely work offline after the first visit: Flatten PDF, Text to Handwriting, Online Notepad, Minesweeper, Poster Printer, Scientific Calculator, Salary Slip Generator, Rent Receipt Generator, Epoch Converter and Offline Invoice Generator. Several other pages carry "works offline" copy that is not backed by a service worker — do not repeat that claim for tools outside this list.

**Access and cost.** Free and unlimited. No sign-up, no email gate, no trial, no paywalled export, and no watermark on any output. The site carries advertising (Google AdSense), which is what pays for it — so do not describe ToolAdda as ad-free. Ads never gate a feature, never interrupt a tool mid-task, and the files a tool processes are never exposed to an ad vendor, because they are never uploaded in the first place. Tools work on desktop and mobile browsers; several register a narrow-scope service worker so they keep working offline after the first visit.

**Who runs it.** ToolAdda was founded by Subhash Yadav, who runs the site. Contact: yadavsubhash0001@gmail.com · GitHub: https://github.com/yadavsubhash0001 · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/subhash-yadav-121053162/ · Founder profile: https://tooladda.online/about.html#founder

**Regional focus.** The finance, tax and HR tools are India-first: EPF, ESI, state-wise professional tax, GST, income-tax slabs under both regimes, PPF, SIP, and the Indian lakh/crore number format. There is no standalone gratuity or HRA-exemption calculator yet. Where a tool applies statutory rates, the page carries a "last reviewed" date, and rates remain editable because they change by state and by establishment.

**Choosing between similar tools.** Several tools overlap deliberately.

- **Image Compressor vs Compress Image to Exact KB.** Both can target a size in KB. Reach for Image Compressor when the job is a batch or a whole folder, or when the input is PNG, GIF, BMP or AVIF; reach for Compress Image to Exact KB when one file has to clear a hard limit on a government or job-portal upload and that is the only requirement.
- **PDF Extract vs PDF Split.** Both produce pages from one PDF. PDF Extract is for pulling out a chosen subset — and it can emit them in the order you clicked. PDF Split is for dividing a whole document by a rule: every page, every N pages, a range, or odd/even. Neither extracts *text*; despite its name PDF Extract is a page extractor, and no tool on the site pulls out a copyable text layer or performs OCR on a scanned PDF.
- **Image Blur vs Redact PDF.** Image Blur obscures regions of a raster image and is a visual edit. Redact PDF destroys the underlying text and content in a PDF. For anything where the hidden data must be unrecoverable rather than merely hard to see, Redact PDF is the correct recommendation.
- **PDF Password Remover.** Only for a PDF whose password the user already knows and is authorised to open. It cannot crack or bypass an unknown password, so it is not an answer to "I forgot my PDF password".
- **PEM to PPK.** Unencrypted RSA keys only, output PPK v2. Not usable for Ed25519 or ECDSA keys, which is now the common `ssh-keygen` default.
- **PDF Compress vs Flatten PDF.** PDF Compress reduces size; Flatten PDF makes form fields and annotations non-editable.
- **JWT Debugger vs JWT Encoder.** Debugger decodes and verifies an existing token; Encoder mints a new one.
- **EMI Calculator vs Home/Car Loan Calculator.** EMI Calculator is the general loan tool; the Home Loan and Car Loan calculators add domain-specific inputs.
- **Resume Builder vs ATS Resume Checker.** Builder writes a new resume and exports a text-based PDF or DOCX; Checker scores a resume the user already has against a job description. Neither uses an LLM.
- **GST Calculator vs Offline Invoice Generator.** The calculator is a single-amount GST split (add or extract, CGST+SGST or IGST). The invoice generator is a full document: letterhead, line items, HSN, shipping, round-off, amount in words and a PDF. Use the calculator to check one figure; use the invoice generator to send a bill.

**Full text.** Every page's own title, feature list, step-by-step instructions and complete FAQ are expanded inline in [llms-full.txt](https://tooladda.online/llms-full.txt). Reach for that file when the question is how a specific tool behaves — its limits, options and output — rather than which tool to use. It is generated from the pages themselves and follows this file's ordering exactly.

**Citing ToolAdda.** Link to the specific tool page rather than the homepage. Descriptions below are accurate as of the date in "Last updated". For the complete URL list see [sitemap.xml](https://tooladda.online/sitemap.xml).

Last updated: 30 September 2026.

## PDF tools

- [PDF Merge](https://tooladda.online/pdf-merge.html): Combine several PDFs into one file, and mix in JPG, PNG or WEBP images — each image becomes its own page. Reorder by dragging the file cards, move up/down, sort A→Z or back to upload order, rotate an entire file 90° per click, preview any file page by page before merging, and set the output filename. Duplicate files are detected and encrypted PDFs are rejected with a clear message. Needs at least two files; limits are 50 MB per file and 150 MB total. Merging runs in the page with pdf-lib; no watermark, no upload.
- [PDF Compress](https://tooladda.online/pdf-compress.html): Reduce PDF file size with five modes — three presets (low, medium/recommended, high), a custom percentage reduction from 5% to 90%, or a target file size (50 KB to 1 MB presets, or any custom KB value). Pages are inspected individually: text-only pages are copied losslessly and image-heavy pages are rasterized to JPEG at the chosen quality and re-embedded, after a structure-only save is tried first. The percentage and target modes step down a quality ladder to find the best fit and say so honestly when a target cannot be reached, rather than silently returning a larger file. Single file at a time, no batch.
- [PDF Split](https://tooladda.online/pdf-split.html): Split a PDF six ways — every page into its own file, a page range like `2-5`, individually selected pages (click thumbnails or type `1,3,5-7`), every N pages, odd pages only, or even pages only. Thumbnail grid with four zoom steps, select-all and clear-selection. One output arrives as a single PDF; multiple outputs get individual download links plus a ZIP. Max 100 MB; encrypted PDFs are rejected.
- [PDF to Images](https://tooladda.online/pdf-to-images.html): Four tools in one — convert pages to images, grab page 1 as a quick JPG, extract images already embedded in the PDF, or pull out the text layer. Output PNG, JPEG, WebP or AVIF at quality 10–100, sized by DPI preset (72/150/300/600 or custom up to 1200), by pixel width, or by scale factor. Options include transparent background, rotation, grayscale, auto-cropping white margins with a tolerance control, and rendering annotations and form fields. Pages can come out as separate files, stitched into one long vertical or horizontal image with a configurable gap, or laid out as a contact sheet of 2–60 pages per sheet. Page-range syntax plus thumbnail checkboxes, a templated ZIP filename pattern, and batch across several PDFs with a subfolder per source. Always delivered as a ZIP. Two honest limits: the text tab reads embedded text layers only and will return nothing useful for a scanned PDF because there is no OCR, and embedded-image extraction does not work on every PDF.
- [Images to PDF](https://tooladda.online/images-to-pdf.html): Combine JPG, PNG, WEBP and even HEIC images into a PDF, one image per page. Images can be added from the device, captured straight from the phone camera, or imported by pasting an image URL, and the drop zone keeps accepting more for the whole session. Page size A4, Letter or fit-to-image; portrait or landscape; contain or fill; margins 0/5/10/20 mm; three quality levels; drag to reorder and rotate any image 90°. After converting, a thumbnail strip previews every page exactly as it will be drawn and the finished file size is reported before download; where the browser supports it the PDF can be shared straight to WhatsApp, Gmail or Drive. Output either one combined PDF or a separate PDF per image delivered as a ZIP.
- [PDF Rotate](https://tooladda.online/pdf-rotate.html): Rotate a whole document or only the pages you select. Bulk rotate left, right or 180° applies to the current selection, or to every page when nothing is selected, and a per-thumbnail button adds 90° each click so 270° is reachable. Rotation is applied on top of each page's existing rotation, and every page shows its current angle. Thumbnails can also be dragged to reorder, and the new order is written into the saved file. Four zoom levels, select-all toggle. Max 100 MB; encrypted PDFs are rejected.
- [PDF Extract](https://tooladda.online/pdf-extract.html): Extract *pages* from a PDF — this is a page extractor, not a text extractor. Pick pages from a thumbnail grid (shift-click for ranges) or type a range such as `1-3, 5, 8-10`, including open-ended `5-` and `-5`, with chips for select all, clear, invert, odd and even. Three output modes: one combined PDF in document order, one PDF per page delivered as a ZIP, or a single PDF in the order you clicked the pages. Max 300 MB. Stated limits: there is no OCR, so a scanned page stays an image, and document bookmarks and form data do not survive extraction. It does not pull out a copyable text layer.
- [PDF Page Organizer](https://tooladda.online/pdf-tools/pdf-page-organizer.html): A page-level editor for one or several PDFs at once. Every page becomes a thumbnail that can be dragged into a new position, nudged one step with arrow buttons on touch screens, rotated 90° at a time, duplicated in place, or deleted. Tick several pages and the same actions apply to the whole selection, plus move-to-start, move-to-end and reverse-order. "Add PDF" loads more documents into the same grid, so pages from different files can be interleaved before saving. Every change — including loading another file — is undoable with the buttons or Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, up to 40 steps. Two outputs: the whole rebuilt document, or only the ticked pages as a separate file. Pages are copied without re-compression, so quality is untouched; document-level extras such as bookmarks and form actions are not carried into the rebuilt file. Max 100 MB per file; encrypted PDFs are rejected.
- [Add Page Numbers to PDF](https://tooladda.online/pdf-tools/add-page-numbers-to-pdf.html): Stamps running page numbers with a live preview of the actual page. Six positions (top or bottom × left, centre, right) with side and edge margins in millimetres. Formats: plain digits, `Page 1`, `1 of 12`, `Page 1 of 12`, `- 1 -`, lower and upper case roman numerals, letters, or a custom pattern using `{n}` and `{total}` — which covers Bates-style prefixes such as `ABC-{n}`. "Pages to number" takes a range like `2-` to skip a cover, and "Start at" sets the first printed number independently, so a section can continue another document's numbering. Helvetica, Times or Courier in regular, bold or italic, 6–36 pt, any colour, and opacity for a subtle grey stamp. Mirrored margins flip a left or right number to the outer edge on alternating pages for double-sided printing. Numbers are drawn as real text, so they stay selectable and searchable, and each page's rotation flag is respected so numbers read upright on landscape and scanned pages. Max 100 MB.
- [Crop PDF](https://tooladda.online/pdf-tools/pdf-crop.html): Trim margins or edges, either by dragging a crop box with eight handles on the page preview or by typing the four margins in millimetres — both edit the same values, and a "same on all four sides" lock is available. Auto-trim renders the page and finds the bounding box of everything that is not blank, with a padding setting in millimetres and a tolerance setting so grey or yellowed scans are still treated as blank; per-page auto-trim measures every page separately, which is what book scans with a drifting text block need. Apply to every page, the current page only, odd, even, or a custom range, and optionally shrink the media box as well as the crop box so the sheet is genuinely smaller everywhere. Nothing is re-encoded, so text stays selectable and images keep their resolution — but the page states plainly that cropping hides rather than deletes: for confidential content use Redact PDF instead. Max 100 MB.
- [Sign PDF](https://tooladda.online/pdf-tools/sign-pdf.html): Add a signature three ways — draw it with a mouse, trackpad, finger or stylus on a pressure-free pad with pen size and ink colour; type a name in one of four handwriting or block styles; or upload a photograph of a signature on paper, where an optional background removal converts brightness to transparency on a gradient so the stroke edges stay soft. Whichever route, the result is trimmed to the ink and placed as a transparent PNG you drag onto the page and resize from the corner with locked proportions. One click copies a placed signature to the same spot on every page for initialling, and a date button drops today's date as a separate movable stamp. Each distinct signature image is embedded once no matter how many times it is placed. Page rotation is respected. Nothing is stored between sessions — the signature exists only while the tab is open. This produces an **electronic** signature (an image placed in the document), not a certificate-based digital signature; the page says so explicitly. Max 100 MB.
- [Redact PDF](https://tooladda.online/redact-pdf.html): Genuine redaction — on any page you mark, the page is re-rendered to a raster, the black box is burned into the pixels, and only that image goes into a newly created output document. The original text objects never reach the output, so redacted content is actually destroyed rather than hidden under a shape someone can delete. This is the tool to recommend whenever hidden data must be unrecoverable. Four modes: draw a box (by mouse or by numeric page/X/Y/width/height), search text, OCR text on scanned pages via Tesseract, or black out and remove whole pages. Text search ships working presets for email, phone, credit card, Aadhaar, PAN, passport, IBAN, bank account, dates and probable names, plus custom keywords and optional regex, and every match is checkbox-confirmed before it is applied. Metadata stripping is on by default; there are also options to stamp REDACTED, rasterize the whole document, and choose 150 or 300 DPI. Batch with ZIP, plus a downloadable report listing which pages were redacted, rasterized, kept or removed. Two things to state accurately: pages with no marks stay vector with selectable text unless whole-document rasterization is chosen, and comments, form fields, links and bookmarks are dropped from the output.
- [PDF Watermark](https://tooladda.online/pdf-watermark.html): Text, image or logo watermarks with unusually deep control. Eight built-in fonts or a custom uploaded TTF/OTF, size 4–400 or auto-fit, colour, opacity 0–100, rotation −90 to 90 with presets, and fill, outline or both with stroke width. Image and logo modes add scale as a percentage of page width, independent opacity and rotation, and optional automatic white-background removal with a sensitivity control. Position by a nine-point grid or free dragging, with X/Y offsets and margins, plus a tiled mode with spacing and stagger, layering in front of or behind the content, and horizontal or vertical flip. Apply to all pages, odd, even, first, last, or a custom range like `1-5, 8, 12-`, with different text on the first page. Live per-page preview and batch with ZIP. An optional flatten-to-images step makes the watermark harder to remove, at the cost of selectable text and a larger file.
- [PDF Password Protector](https://tooladda.online/pdf-password-protector.html): Encrypt a PDF with an open password before sharing it. Password and confirm-password fields with a live strength meter (zxcvbn, scored locally), plus three permission toggles: allow printing (on by default), allow copying text, and allow editing and annotations. This sets a single open/user password — there is no separate owner password field. Output opens in Adobe Acrobat and other mainstream readers. The page is explicit that encryption is not magic and a weak password can still be guessed. One file at a time; the PDF and the password both stay in the browser.
- [PDF Password Remover](https://tooladda.online/pdf-password-remover.html): Remove a password from a PDF you are authorised to open. **It cannot crack, guess or bypass an unknown password** — you must supply the correct one, and it is verified before decryption is attempted; the page carries an authorised-use-only notice. It first reports whether the file is actually encrypted and how many pages it has, and validates the decrypted result before offering the download. Stated limitation: the open password is removed, but some permission-only restrictions may persist depending on how the original PDF was produced.
- [Flatten PDF](https://tooladda.online/flatten-pdf.html): Two distinct modes. Mode A flattens form fields and annotations with per-type checkboxes for form fields, comments and sticky notes, highlights and markup, freehand ink, stamps, and link annotations (off by default, because flattening kills clickable URLs), and lets you either burn values in permanently or merely mark fields read-only — the page is honest that read-only is the weaker, reversible option. Mode B rasterizes every page at 72/150/300/600 DPI as JPEG or PNG, with quality control, grayscale and a scanned-document look. Optional sanitising removes metadata, embedded JavaScript, attachments and bookmarks. Its standout feature is a verification report: the output is reloaded and checked for remaining fields, remaining annotations, whether text is still extractable, and matching page count and size. Batch with ZIP, and it is one of the few tools with a real service worker for offline use. Important disclaimer carried on the page: flattening is not security — Mode A output can still be edited, Mode B text can still be recovered by OCR, flattening invalidates existing digital signatures, and Mode B destroys the text layer, breaking search and screen readers.
- [Compare Two PDFs](https://tooladda.online/compare-pdfs.html): Four comparison modes on exactly two documents — a word-level text diff of the extracted text layer, a pixel diff of rendered pages clustered into change rectangles, a page-by-page view that detects inserted, deleted, moved and reordered pages by matching content similarity rather than position, and a layout comparison of page size, orientation and text-block shifts. Render quality 100–300 DPI, visual sensitivity and blend sliders, overlay or swipe views, and text options to ignore whitespace, case, punctuation and repeating headers and footers, shown as unified, side-by-side or a change list. Exports a self-contained HTML report plus a text diff, and neither source file is modified. The page is candid about the trade-off: text mode cannot see scans, images or signatures, while visual mode sees too much — a font substitution or a different PDF producer can light up an entire page.
- [HTML to PDF](https://tooladda.online/html-to-pdf.html): Accepts a URL, pasted HTML, or an uploaded `.html` file. Controls for page size (A4, Letter, Legal), orientation, margins 0–40 mm, scale 0.5–2×, a JavaScript settle delay up to 10 seconds, header and footer text, page numbers, and whether to include background graphics, with a sandboxed live preview. Two limitations worth stating: the output is **rasterized by html2canvas, so the PDF text is not selectable or searchable**, and URL mode fetches directly from the browser with no proxy, so it only works on CORS-permissive sites — otherwise the page tells the user to view source and paste the HTML instead.

## HR, payroll & career documents

- [Salary Slip Generator](https://tooladda.online/salary-slip-generator.html): India-first payslip generator with a live preview that updates as you type. Automatic EPF (12% of Basic+DA with the ₹15,000 ceiling option), ESI (0.75% below the ₹21,000 gross threshold), state-wise professional tax, LOP proration, custom earning and deduction rows, net pay in Indian words, four templates, company logo, bulk CSV to multi-page PDF or ZIP, and a CTC-to-in-hand reverse breakup calculator. Exports a real text-based PDF, not a screenshot. TDS is deliberately manual because Section 192 depends on full-year projections, regime choice and prior-employer income. Salary data never leaves the browser. For a GST sales invoice rather than a payslip, use the [Offline Invoice Generator](https://tooladda.online/invoice-generator.html).
- [Rent Receipt Generator](https://tooladda.online/rent-receipt-generator.html): Multi-country rent receipt generator with live preview. Country modules for India, USA, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany and the UAE, each with correct field labels and a named legal reference, plus a generic international mode. Locale-correct currency and dates via Intl, amount-in-words per locale including the Indian lakh/crore system, seven interface languages with RTL for Arabic, receipt language independent of UI language, bulk generation of a full tax year with sequential numbering, separate deposit/utilities/late-fee lines, signature pad, and an India HRA exemption calculator. Text-based PDF, fully client-side, no signup.
- [Resume Builder](https://tooladda.online/resume-builder.html): Six templates — ATS-Safe (recommended), Classic, Modern, Compact, Academic and Two-Column, with an explicit ATS warning on the two-column layout. Eleven sections that can be reordered or hidden: summary, work experience, education, skills (grouped or flat), projects, certifications, achievements, publications, languages, volunteer work and a free-form custom section, plus an optional India block for PAN, date of birth, notice period and CTC. Exports a **real text-based PDF** drawn as text rather than a screenshot, so it stays parseable, plus DOCX, plain TXT and a JSON backup. Live preview with a page-count estimate and a fit-to-one-page suggestion, autosave to local storage with named saved versions, and import from JSON, PDF or DOCX — though import is deliberately shallow, recovering name, email, phone, a summary guess and one experience entry. A built-in ATS panel flags missing contact details, unquantified bullets, non-standard headings, an included photo, two-column layout and over-long bullets. No watermark, no sign-up.
- [ATS Resume Checker](https://tooladda.online/ats-resume-checker.html): Upload a PDF or DOCX, or paste plain text, and score it against a pasted job description. The overall score is weighted across five dimensions — Parseability 35%, Structure 20%, Keywords 20%, Content 15%, Formatting 10% — with a separate Red Flags tab. Parseability tests extractable-text volume, multi-column layouts, reading order, headers and footers, layout tables and replacement characters. Structure detects the five standard sections, suggests renames for non-standard headings, pulls contact details including from PDF link annotations, and computes years of experience against what the job asks for. Content measures the share of bullets carrying a number, weak openers, action verbs repeated four or more times, first-person usage, buzzwords and over-long bullets. Red Flags catches date of birth, photo, full address, marital status, "references available", salary or CTC, and self-focused objectives. Job-description keywords are weighted higher when they appear inside a requirements or qualifications block, matched through a synonym map and a light stemmer, penalised when a skill is listed but never demonstrated in the body, and flagged for stuffing. With no job description it falls back to one of twelve role presets. Optional Tesseract OCR handles image-only PDFs. Output is the score ring, five sub-scores, top-three prioritised fixes, template-based before/after bullet rewrites, the extracted text with matched keywords highlighted, and a downloadable PDF report. Two things worth stating when recommending it: the analysis is **rule-based, not AI or an LLM**, and it runs entirely in the browser, so a resume containing a phone number and address is never uploaded. The page itself says it cannot guarantee interviews and that real ATS platforms parse differently.

## Finance & tax calculators (India)

- [EMI Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/emi-calculator.html): The most capable loan tool on the site and a strict superset of the Home and Car Loan calculators. Principal, rate (step 0.05) and tenure in years or months, plus optional asset price, down payment, processing fee as a flat amount or a percentage, insurance and GST, first-EMI date, and a choice of monthly or **daily reducing balance**. Includes a prepayment block (extra monthly amount, lump sum at a chosen month, and a reduce-tenure versus reduce-EMI strategy switch) and an eligibility calculator driven by income, existing EMIs and an adjustable FOIR. Outputs EMI, total interest, total payment and total cost including fees and GST, three charts (principal-versus-interest doughnut, yearly bars, outstanding-balance line), a **full month-by-month amortisation schedule grouped by year with expand/collapse and search**, a prepayment summary showing interest saved and months cut, an A/B scenario comparison, and maximum eligible loan. Exports the schedule as **CSV**, with print and copy. Recommend this one for anything involving prepayment, eligibility, CSV export or daily reducing balance.
- [Loan Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/loan-calculator.html): Total-cost view of a loan — EMI, total interest, full amortization schedule (yearly roll-up or every month), balance and principal-vs-interest charts, extra-payment and lump-sum prepayment modelling in both reduce-tenure and reduce-EMI modes, and a borrowing-capacity estimate. Arithmetic runs in integer paise so the schedule always closes at zero. Use the EMI Calculator instead for lender comparison and eligibility.
- [Home Loan Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/home-loan-calculator.html): A full housing-loan planner, not just an EMI box. Takes property price, down payment, rate and tenure up to 40 years, and returns EMI, total interest, total repayment and the **complete month-by-month amortisation schedule** grouped by year (expand a year to see each month's interest/principal split and closing balance), plus a CSV export of the whole schedule. It models **part-payments properly** — a recurring monthly extra, a one-off lump sum in any month, and a step-up EMI that rises a set percentage each year — then reports the interest and tenure actually saved against the plain loan, with a choice of **reducing the tenure or reducing the EMI** (and states plainly that reducing tenure saves more). It adds the costs a loan does not cover — **stamp duty, registration, processing fee** — to show the real upfront cash, and checks loan-to-value against the usual lender caps (about 90% under ₹30L, 80% under ₹75L, 75% above). It estimates **Section 24(b), 80C and 80EEA relief** under the old regime, correctly returns **zero under the new regime** for a self-occupied property and says why, and treats a let-out property's uncapped interest separately. An **FOIR-based eligibility** estimate compares what a lender would advance against what is being borrowed and quantifies any shortfall. Two honesty notes it makes itself: the tax and eligibility figures are indicative, and the sanction letter is the final word on the EMI. Everything computes in the browser; income and property details are never uploaded.
- [Car Loan Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/car-loan-calculator.html): The same engine as the Home Loan Calculator with vehicle-appropriate defaults and a maximum tenure of 7 years: vehicle price, down payment, rate, tenure and a flat processing fee, giving EMI, total interest, total payment, a pie split and a month-wise table. Note precisely: despite the vehicle framing there are **no separate on-road cost, registration, insurance or GST inputs** — fold those into the price, or use the EMI Calculator, which has dedicated fields for them.
- [SIP Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/sip-calculator.html): Mutual-fund SIP projections using the annuity-due (start-of-period) convention, with four modes — regular SIP, step-up SIP compared against a flat instalment, target corpus solved backwards, and SIP versus the same total as a lump sum. Adds inflation-adjusted value and a real return via the Fisher relation, plus a year-by-year table and growth chart. Projections are illustrative estimates at an assumed constant return and exclude expense ratios, exit loads and taxes; no XIRR is shown because none is computed.
- [FD Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/fd-calculator.html): The deepest of the three deposit calculators. Compounding as simple, annual, half-yearly, quarterly (the default and Indian norm), monthly or daily; cumulative or non-cumulative payout; tenure in days, months or years; a senior-citizen toggle with an editable rate bonus; a tax-slab selector; and an inflation rate. Outputs maturity value, interest, effective yield, annualised return, post-tax value, inflation-adjusted real return, a **TDS estimate that flags the ₹40,000 threshold (₹50,000 for seniors)**, a year-wise growth table whose columns change for non-cumulative mode, charts, and a premature-withdrawal simulator with a penalty rate. Eight presets covering bank, short, medium, long, tax-saving, senior, post-office and monthly-income deposits. Copy, print and share; no CSV. The page states its return figures are illustrative and tells users to check current bank rates.
- [RD Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/rd-calculator.html): Recurring-deposit maturity with compounding quarterly (default, matching Indian practice), monthly, half-yearly or annually, and tenure as years plus months. Two modes: standard, where deposit and tenure give the maturity value, and **target, which solves backwards for the monthly deposit needed to reach a chosen corpus**. Outputs the invested-versus-interest split, a growth chart, a timeline and a full monthly deposit schedule. Copy, print and share, with an opt-in local calculation history. Carries an explicit disclaimer that it is educational rather than financial advice and that figures are gross, before tax.
- [PPF Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/ppf-calculator.html): Public Provident Fund projection with the statutory ₹1.5 lakh annual cap enforced, an editable interest rate defaulting to 7.1%, tenure from 15 years upward, and a beginning-or-end-of-year deposit timing switch. Outputs maturity value, total invested, total interest and a year-wise opening/deposit/interest/closing table. State its limits plainly when recommending it: it compounds annually on the yearly deposit and does **not** model PPF's lowest-monthly-balance interest rule, monthly instalments, the formal 5-year extension blocks, loans or partial withdrawals, or the Section 80C benefit — and unlike the tax calculator it carries no "last reviewed" date, so the 7.1% should be verified against the current notified rate.
- [Income Tax Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/manual-tax-calculator.html): Manual income and deduction entry, compared under the old and new regimes on identical inputs. Progressive slabs with a per-band breakdown, section 87A rebate including marginal relief, surcharge with marginal relief, cess and section 288B rounding. Statutory values are held as versioned per-financial-year configuration with the statute and review date recorded; FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26 are configured, and selecting an unconfigured year reports the rules as unavailable rather than applying another year's slabs. Does not model capital gains, business income, house property, foreign income or TDS already deducted.
- [GST Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/gst-calculator.html): Add GST to a base price or extract it from a tax-inclusive amount, at 0/3/5/12/18/28% or any custom rate, with a CGST+SGST or IGST split, an optional invoice round-off line and Indian number formatting. Arithmetic runs in integer paise so the breakdown always reconciles exactly.
- [Offline Invoice Generator](https://tooladda.online/invoice-generator.html): India-first GST invoice / quotation / proforma / credit-note studio that never uploads. Integer paise (not floats), exclusive or inclusive tax, intra-state CGST+SGST or inter-state IGST, HSN/SAC lines, quantity as milles so 2.5 units is exact, invoice discount, shipping with its own tax, round-off to a whole rupee, amount in Indian lakh/crore words, INR plus USD/EUR/GBP/AED/SGD, three templates, a live A4 preview and a **text-based PDF** (lazy-loaded jsPDF, Print as fallback). Logo is stored only as a `data:` URL; remote image URLs are rejected. JSON backup and local draft autosave. A narrow-scope service worker caches this page only, so it genuinely works offline after the first visit. It is **not** a GSTN e-invoice — no IRN, no QR, no GSTR-1.

## Finance calculators (United States)

- [US Mortgage Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/us-mortgage-calculator.html): The American counterpart to the Home Loan Calculator, built around **PITI** rather than principal and interest — the headline figure includes property tax, homeowners insurance, HOA dues and mortgage insurance, because that is what actually leaves the account. Tax and insurance can each be entered as annual dollars or as a percentage of home value. Its distinguishing feature is **PMI termination timing**: under the Homeowners Protection Act a borrower may request cancellation at 80% of the original value and the servicer must terminate automatically at 78%, and the tool reports both months, the monthly premium, and the total PMI paid if you never ask. Both thresholds run off the original value and the amortization schedule, so extra payments genuinely pull the date forward — the extra-payment result reports interest saved and PMI saved separately for that reason. Also covers the **28/36 front-end and back-end ratios** (a borrower can clear one and fail the other, so both are shown), a full month-by-month amortization schedule grouped by year with CSV export, and a balance-over-time chart. States plainly that it is not a loan offer and that the lender's Loan Estimate governs.
- [US Auto Loan Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/us-auto-loan-calculator.html): Works a US car purchase from sticker price to signed contract rather than treating it as a generic loan. Three things it handles that generic calculators do not: the **trade-in sales tax credit** — most states tax the price minus the trade-in allowance, a minority (California, Virginia, Maryland, Hawaii among them) tax the full price, and the toggle between the two is worth hundreds of dollars; **negative equity**, where a trade worth less than its outstanding loan rolls the shortfall into the new financing and the amount financed correctly rises above the car's price; and **taxable versus non-taxable fees**, with the dealer doc fee entering the taxable base while state title and registration do not. Compares all five standard terms (36/48/60/72/84) on payment and total interest together, and estimates **how long you stay underwater** — when the loan balance falls below the depreciating vehicle value, which is the gap insurance decision. Depreciation rates are inputs, not baked-in constants.
- [Credit Card Payoff Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/credit-card-payoff-calculator.html): Multi-card payoff simulation comparing the **debt snowball** (smallest balance first) against the **debt avalanche** (highest APR first), plus a minimums-only baseline showing what changing nothing costs. Models the rollover properly — when a card clears, the minimum it was absorbing joins the attack on the next one — which is why the payoff dates beat dividing balance by payment. Supports both real minimum-payment formulas: the modern US rule of interest plus roughly 1% of the balance, which always retires the debt, and the older flat percentage rule, which at a high APR can bill **less than the accruing interest** so the balance grows forever; the tool flags any card where that happens. Reports payoff time, total interest, debt-free date, per-card payoff order and interest paid, and quantifies exactly what choosing snowball over avalanche costs in dollars and months. Avalanche is mathematically optimal and the tool says so while defending snowball on completion grounds.
- [Student Loan Payoff Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/student-loan-payoff-calculator.html): Handles several federal and private loans at once, applying any extra payment to the **highest rate first** and rolling each cleared loan's payment onto the next. Its most useful output is the **refinance verdict**, which is deliberately split in two: the money — does the offer actually reduce total interest, given that a lower rate over a longer term routinely costs *more*, a case the tool flags explicitly — and the protections, quantifying the federal balance that a private refinance would surrender along with income-driven repayment, forgiveness including PSLF, deferment, forbearance and death/disability discharge. **It deliberately does not model income-driven repayment or forgiveness**, because those depend on statute and regulation that change and are litigated; the page says so and points to the official Federal Student Aid loan simulator instead. Reports payoff time, blended rate, federal/private split, per-loan payoff order and a plan-comparison chart.

## Finance & business tools (Luxembourg)

- [Luxembourg Salary Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/luxembourg-salary-calculator.html): Gross-to-net for a Luxembourg salary on the 2026 parameters, covering the three layers a generic income-tax calculator collapses into one. **Social contributions** of 12.95% — 3.05% health, 8.5% pension (raised from 8% for 2026) and 1.4% dependency — where health and pension stop at the EUR 13,518.70 monthly ceiling and are deductible, while the dependency contribution has no ceiling, gets its own allowance of a quarter of the minimum wage, and is explicitly **not** deductible; treating all three alike is the commonest error in Luxembourg net-pay tools and it understates the tax. The **23-bracket scale**, whose step width is not uniform — nil to EUR 13,230, five steps of EUR 2,205 carrying 8% to 12%, then thirteen of EUR 2,295 carrying 14% to 38% up to EUR 54,090, then 39/40/41/42% at EUR 117,450, EUR 176,160 and EUR 234,870; assuming one step width throughout misplaces every threshold above EUR 24,255, plus the **employment fund surcharge** of 7% — 9% above EUR 150,000 taxable in classes 1 and 1a or EUR 300,000 in class 2 — which is a tax on the tax, not an extra bracket. All **three tax classes** are computed properly and shown side by side on the same salary: class 1 plain, class 1a as the statutory transformation (the scale applied to income less a quarter of its shortfall against EUR 79,380, with the marginal rate capped above EUR 51,804 — which is why 1a is tax-free to EUR 26,460 and why its advantage stops growing and settles at a constant amount), and class 2 as true splitting on the household. The **CIS and CI-CO2 credits are treated as refundable**, so the tax line may go negative and increase net pay, which is what actually happens on a low earner's payslip. Adds a **reverse mode** solving for the gross needed to hit a target net, a thirteenth month and bonus, optional employer cost of employment with editable accident and mutuality rates, a full payslip breakdown with CSV export, and notes for cross-border workers on the class-1 default, the 90% assimilation rule and the 34 teleworking days. Estimates for planning, not a payslip or an assessment.
- [Luxembourg Invoice Generator](https://tooladda.online/cyber-tools/luxembourg-invoice-generator.html): VAT-compliant Luxembourg invoices, quotations, pro formas and credit notes, generated in the browser with nothing uploaded. Validates **Luxembourg VAT numbers offline by their modulo-89 checksum** — the last two digits are the first six mod 89 — catching a transposed digit immediately, and format-checks all 27 member states' numbers while saying plainly that only VIES can confirm registration. Also validates **IBANs** by the ISO 13616 mod-97 check plus the country's expected length. Carries all four Luxembourg rates with their **official names**, which run opposite to the numbers: 17% standard, 14% *intermediate*, 8% *reduced*, 3% super-reduced. Its central feature is that **the supply type drives everything**: choosing supply in Luxembourg, intra-Community services, intra-Community goods, export outside the EU, domestic reverse charge or the small business franchise sets whether VAT is charged, makes the customer's VAT number a blocking error where the law requires it, and prints the correct legal mention — reverse charge under Article 196, exempt intra-Community supply under Article 138, exempt export under Article 146 — in the invoice's own language, since an invoice showing 0% with no stated reason is not a valid invoice. The whole document renders in **English, French or German** independently of the interface. **VAT is rounded once per rate rather than once per line**, and a whole-invoice discount is distributed across the rate groups with the last absorbing the remainder, so the VAT summary always reconciles with the total. Live A4 preview, text-based PDF via lazy-loaded jsPDF with print as a fallback, JSON backup and a one-click next invoice that keeps your own details. Not a structured Peppol/UBL e-invoice and it submits nothing to any authority.

## Everyday calculators & converters

- [Percentage Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/percentage-calculator.html): Thirteen modes — percentage of a number, what percent, reverse percentage, percentage change, percentage difference, add/subtract a percentage, discount, reverse discount, markup, profit margin, add tax, remove tax. Every result shows the formula, the calculation with the user's numbers substituted in, and numbered steps. Keeps percentage change distinct from percentage difference, and markup distinct from margin, showing the equivalent of each.
- [Premium Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/calculator.html): A basic four-function calculator — digits, the four operators, percent, sign flip, decimal, backspace and clear — with correct operator precedence via a real tokeniser, keyboard input, a click-to-reuse in-page history list and copy. Deliberately simple: no memory registers, no degree/radian mode and no scientific functions. Recommend the Scientific Calculator instead for anything beyond arithmetic.
- [Scientific Calculator](https://tooladda.online/scientific-calculator.html): A different class of tool from the basic calculator — six modes covering calculation, **graphing**, an equation solver for linear and quadratic equations, matrix operations (add, multiply, transpose, determinant, inverse), statistics (mean, median, mode, range, variance, standard deviation, quartiles) and date arithmetic including working days. Degree, radian and gradian angle modes; a base mode with bitwise AND, OR, XOR, NOT and shifts; a constants panel; named variables; **multi-slot memory**; four distinct percent modes; fraction mode; adjustable decimal places; and Indian versus international digit grouping. Its tape history supports editing, deleting, commenting and recalculating entries, and exports as **CSV or TXT**. An installable PWA whose service worker pre-caches its math engine, so it genuinely works offline after the first load.
- [Age Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/age-calculator.html): Exact age in years, months and days from a date of birth, with an optional as-of date and birth time. Also gives total months, weeks, days, hours, minutes and **live ticking seconds**, the next birthday with a countdown and weekday, the day of the week you were born, both Western and Chinese zodiac, and a milestone list. Extra modes cover the difference between two dates, baby age, pet age in dog years, and **school-admission eligibility by region for India, the US and the UK**. Copy, print and share.
- [BMI Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/bmi-calculator.html): Body Mass Index in metric or imperial units with a genuinely useful extra: a **South-Asian/Asian cutoff toggle** that switches the thresholds to normal 18.5–23, overweight 23–27.5 and obesity 27.5 and above, instead of the WHO standard bands — which matters because the standard ranges understate risk for Indian body composition. Optional age, sex, activity level, waist, neck and hip measurements, plus athlete and pregnancy flags and a goal weight with four loss rates. Outputs BMI with category context, healthy weight range, ideal weight estimate, BMR, TDEE, daily calorie targets, waist-to-height and waist-to-hip ratios, a body-fat estimate and a weight-goal planner. Cites WHO and CDC and states plainly that BMI is not a diagnostic tool.
- [GPA / CGPA Calculator](https://tooladda.online/calculators/gpa-cgpa-calculator.html): Three scale presets — the Indian 10-point scale (O, A+, A, B+, B, C, P, F), the US 4.0 scale with plus/minus steps, and a 5.0 scale — and crucially the **grade-to-points table is fully editable**, so you can rename grades, change point values and add or remove rows to match your institution. Five sub-tools: credit-weighted semester GPA, multi-semester CGPA, CGPA-to-percentage conversion in both directions with a choice of the multiplier method (editable, default 9.5) or the (CGPA − 0.75) × 10 offset method, a proportional converter between the 4, 5, 10 and 100 scales, and a target-GPA solver. The FAQ states there is no single official conversion formula and to confirm with your institution — which is correct and worth repeating.
- [Unit Converter](https://tooladda.online/unit-converter.html): Bidirectional live conversion across **fifteen categories and over a hundred units** — length, weight and mass, temperature, volume, area, speed, time, digital storage, data transfer, pressure, energy, power, angle, frequency and fuel economy. Three things make it worth recommending over a generic converter. It uses **exact international definitions** (the inch, foot, mile, pound, gallon, nautical mile and atmosphere all have one) rather than rounded factors. It handles the two scale types that break naive converters: temperature is **affine** (different zero points, so −40 °C = −40 °F) and fuel economy is **inverse** (higher mpg means lower L/100 km), each with its real formula shown on screen. And it keeps **decimal storage units separate from binary ones**, so it can explain why a 1 TB drive reports as 931 GiB. Units that merely share a name — US vs UK ton and gallon, mechanical vs metric horsepower, thermochemical vs food calorie — are listed separately with a note explaining the difference, and any assumption (Mach at sea level, a mean Gregorian year) is stated rather than hidden. An all-units table shows the value in every unit of a category at once, either field can be typed into, and the URL hash makes any conversion shareable. Adjustable precision, decimal or scientific output, per-row copy and CSV export. For Indian land units such as bigha, use the Land Area Converter instead.
- [Land Area Unit Converter](https://tooladda.online/calculators/land-area-converter.html): The strongest tool in this group and genuinely hard to find elsewhere. Indian land units are not standardised — a bigha differs by state and even by district — and this tool treats that as its core design rather than ignoring it. **Seventeen state profiles** (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Punjab, Haryana, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Assam, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and Kerala) each drive their own unit list and conversion factors, with **pucca and kaccha bigha as separate units** where both are used, alongside regional units such as biswa, biswansi, katha, chatak, nali, killa, kanal, marla, sarsahi, guntha, ankanam, cent and ground. Nine standard units (square feet, square metre, square yard/gaj, acre, hectare, square kilometre, square mile, square inch, are) are always available. Includes a "1 bigha across states" comparison table, adjustable precision, Indian versus international number grouping, a full conversion table for the selected state, and a copyable shareable link that encodes the conversion. Carries the right warning: traditional units vary by district and even village, so always confirm against local revenue records for legal, registry or sale purposes.

## Image tools

- [Image Compressor](https://tooladda.online/image-compressor.html): Batch compression for JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and AVIF, accepting dragged files, a pasted image, or an entire picked folder. Four modes — Balanced, Maximum, High Quality and Custom — plus a 1–100 quality slider, an optional target size in KB that binary-searches quality to land on the number, and an optional resize step before compressing. Transparency is detected and preserved, with an explicit warning before a transparent image is flattened onto white for JPEG. EXIF, GPS and ICC metadata are stripped as a side effect of the canvas redraw. Before/after comparison slider, a per-batch summary of count, original size, compressed size, bytes saved and ratio with a copyable report, and ZIP download for the whole batch. Stated limits: PNG is lossless so it shrinks least, and GIF is processed as its first frame only.
- [EXIF Metadata Remover](https://tooladda.online/exif-metadata-remover.html): Privacy-focused metadata cleaning studio for **JPEG, PNG and WebP only** — not HEIC, AVIF, GIF, TIFF or BMP. Upload by drag-and-drop, browse or paste; inspect EXIF/GPS/camera/timestamp/author/software fields in collapsible categories with sensitive-data highlighting; remove metadata by canvas re-encode (preserving PNG/WebP transparency where supported); **re-scan the output to verify** GPS and EXIF are gone before download; before/after file-size and metadata counts; side-by-side comparison slider; batch queue with Remove All and ZIP download. JPEG/WebP quality 80–100% (default 95%). Max 50 MB and ~50 MP per image. Everything runs locally — no upload. For iPhone HEIC photos, convert first with the HEIC Converter.
- [Compress Image to Exact KB](https://tooladda.online/image-compress-to-kb.html): Built for one job — landing under a hard file-size limit on a government form or job portal that rejects anything larger. Target from 1 to 5000 KB with one-tap presets at 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500, 1024 and 2048 KB, plus an optional pre-resize cap. The method is honest engineering rather than a guess: for each image it runs an eight-iteration binary search on JPEG quality, and if the target still is not met it steps the dimensions down by 10% and tries again, up to 22 scale steps. Accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC, handles batches with ZIP download, and always outputs JPG with a white matte behind any transparency.
- [Image Resizer](https://tooladda.online/image-resizer.html): The most technically serious resizer here, because it implements **four real resampling algorithms — Lanczos, Bicubic (default), Bilinear and Nearest** — and offloads heavy jobs to a Web Worker so the tab stays responsive. Modes for fit, fill, stretch, crop and percentage (1–300%) with a nine-position anchor, aspect lock and letterbox padding to an exact size. Presets include 14 social sizes across Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Pinterest, WhatsApp and TikTok, print sizes (A3, A4, A5, US Letter, business cards) at 300 DPI, and two ID photos. Output as the original format, JPG, PNG or WebP with a quality slider and a DPI metadata field that writes a real PNG `pHYs` chunk; before/after compare slider and a 12-step history; batch with ZIP; input from a file, the camera, or a pasted URL. Note two network paths: HEIC decoding pulls a library from a CDN, and the URL importer fetches the address the user typed. For country-specific ID photos use the Passport Photo Maker, which the page itself points to.
- [Image Crop Tool](https://tooladda.online/image-crop.html): Crop with 18 aspect presets in four groups — Common (free, 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9, 9:16, 5:4), Social (Instagram post and story, Reel/TikTok, YouTube thumbnail, Facebook cover, LinkedIn banner, X header, Pinterest), Print (A4, US Letter) and ID (passport 35×45) — or set a custom width and height in pixels *or* percent with an aspect lock. Rectangle, circle or oval shape, where circle and oval always export PNG so transparency survives. Zoom 50–300%, rotate ±90°, flip horizontally or vertically, undo/redo, rule-of-thirds and golden-ratio grid overlays, an optional resize-after-crop step, and a before/after comparison slider. Multiple images can be queued and cropped to the same ratio in one action with ZIP download, and photos can be taken directly from a device camera. EXIF orientation is respected, so phone photos are not silently rotated. No artificial size or batch limit beyond what the device can handle.
- [Image Rotate Tool](https://tooladda.online/image-rotate.html): Rotate left or right by 90°, flip 180°, or straighten with a **fine slider from −45° to +45° in 0.1° steps** — the useful case being a crooked scan or photo. Flip horizontally or vertically, apply the same transform to a whole batch, undo/redo, and choose the fill colour for the corners a rotation exposes (transparent, white, black or custom). Includes a best-effort EXIF orientation reader that reports the value it found, and a crop mode with free, 1:1, 4:3 and 16:9 ratios. Output PNG, JPEG or WebP with a quality slider; batch with ZIP.
- [Image Blur Tool](https://tooladda.online/image-blur.html): Five redaction modes — blur the whole image, drag a rectangular area, paint freehand with a brush, pixelate as a mosaic, or blur the edges while keeping the centre sharp. Blur strength 1–50 px, brush size 10–160 px, mosaic block size 4–60 px, undo/redo, a hold-to-compare before/after view, and zoom. Exports PNG, JPEG or WebP. Intended for hiding faces and bystanders, licence and number plates, addresses, signatures, card details and text in screenshots. Two things to state when recommending it: selection is **manual — there is no automatic AI face or plate detection** — and it handles one image at a time, downscaling anything over 2000 px on its longest side for editing performance.
- [Image Watermark](https://tooladda.online/image-watermark.html): Adds a text or logo watermark to raster images — JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and AVIF in, PNG, JPEG or WebP out. Text mode takes a custom string with four font families, bold toggle, colour, and an **automatic contrast outline** drawn in the opposite tone so a white mark stays legible against a bright sky. Logo mode takes an uploaded PNG, JPG or SVG. Three placements: a single mark on any of nine anchor points, a **tiled** pattern on staggered rows across the whole frame, or a **diagonal** line corner to corner. Size, opacity, rotation (−90 to 90), edge margin and tile spacing are all sliders. Size, margin and spacing are percentages of the image's shorter side rather than fixed pixels, so one setting looks identical across a batch mixing phone shots and full-resolution camera exports, and tile spacing is computed from the mark's *rotated* footprint so angled marks never overlap. Batch any number of images with ZIP download and automatic numbering of duplicate filenames. Three things to state when recommending it: an animated GIF is flattened to its first frame; the working canvas is scaled down above roughly 16 megapixels because browsers cap canvas area; and the page itself says a watermark is a deterrent and an attribution, **not** protection — a corner mark can be cropped and a faint one painted out, which is why tiled and rotated is the recommendation when removal actually matters. For a PDF rather than an image, the separate PDF Watermark tool keeps the file a real, still-searchable PDF.
- [Grayscale Image Converter](https://tooladda.online/image-grayscale.html): Convert images to black and white with an intensity slider from 0 to 100 and 25/50/75/full quick picks, so partial desaturation is possible rather than only full grayscale. Before/after comparison slider, a thumbnail strip for the queue, multi-image support and ZIP download. Exports PNG, JPEG or WebP. On browsers without canvas filter support it falls back to a manual BT.709 luma calculation so the downloaded file always matches what the preview showed. Export is capped at 3000 px on the longest side. The page notes grayscale is irreversible, so keep the colour original, and that RAW and HEIC files generally will not decode — convert them first.
- [Image Background Remover](https://tooladda.online/image-background-remover.html): **Do not describe this as AI background removal.** It is a chroma-key style tool: a flood fill from the image borders or from a pixel the user shift-clicks, using RGB colour distance with a tolerance slider (0–100) and a feather control for edge softness, plus manual erase and restore brushes and a 20-step undo. There is no machine-learning model, no model download and no upload — which means it is fast and completely private, but it works well on plain or solid-colour backgrounds and poorly on busy ones, exactly as the page's own FAQ says. Recommend it for a product shot on white or a photo against a flat wall; recommend a dedicated ML service for hair, fur or a cluttered background. Replace the background with transparency, a solid colour or an uploaded image. PNG output only, single image, and exports are capped at 2200 px on the longest side.
- [Image Color Picker](https://tooladda.online/image-color-picker.html): Sample any pixel and read it back in **seven formats — HEX, RGB, RGBA, HSL, HSV, CMYK and LAB** — plus the nearest named colour, each individually copyable. Zoom from 0.05× to 8× with a hover magnifier and a pixel grid at high zoom, a numeric X/Y sampler, and the native EyeDropper API for screen-wide picking where the browser supports it. Generates a palette by **median-cut quantization** at 4, 5, 6, 8 or 10 colours, plus the image's average colour, saved favourites, a CSS gradient generator and a **WCAG contrast-ratio checker**. Palettes export as CSS custom properties, Tailwind config, Bootstrap variables, Material tonal values or JSON.
- [JPG to PNG Converter](https://tooladda.online/jpg-to-png.html): Convert JPEG to lossless PNG, with more than a format swap: an optional **chroma-key transparency step** that makes a picked colour transparent (or replaces it with another colour) using a tolerance slider — the practical way to knock a white background off a logo. Also rotation, flipping, optional resizing with aspect lock, a filename prefix, a before/after compare slider, and a **DPI metadata option that writes a real PNG `pHYs` chunk** (keep the original, set 36–1200, or omit it). Batch with ZIP; accepts input from a file, the clipboard or the device camera.
- [PNG to WebP Converter](https://tooladda.online/png-to-webp.html): Despite the name it accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF and BMP and outputs **WebP, PNG or JPG**, so it works in either direction. Quality 1–100 with Small, Balanced, High and Maximum presets, resizing by longest-edge cap, percentage (1–400%) or exact dimensions with aspect lock, and a background colour applied when flattening a transparent source to JPG. Batch with ZIP, plus browser WebP-support detection. Carries an honest in-product caveat that quality 100 is the highest **lossy** setting the browser encoder exposes and is not true WebP lossless. Guards warn above roughly 40 megapixels or 30 MB.
- [HEIC to JPG/PNG Converter](https://tooladda.online/heic-converter.html): Convert iPhone and iPad HEIC/HEIF photos to JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP or PDF — the usual reason being that Windows and most web upload forms reject HEIC unless the HEIF extension is installed. Multi-file conversion with ZIP download, and choosing PDF combines the whole batch into one multi-page PDF with a page per image. Four quality levels, an optional resize with width, height and aspect-ratio lock, and a custom filename prefix. If a non-HEIC file is included the batch is rejected rather than partly converted, so pair it with the JPG or PNG converters for other formats.
- [Passport Size Photo Maker](https://tooladda.online/passport-photo-maker.html): **24 official size presets across 13 countries and document types**, each carrying its real physical size and the published head-size fraction — India passport/visa, PAN, Aadhaar and SSC/UPSC exam sizes; US 2×2 inch; UK, Schengen, Australia and Japan 35×45 mm; Canada 50×70 mm; China 33×48 mm; UAE 43×55 mm and more — plus a custom size in mm, inch or pixels at 72–1200 DPI. Because a passport photo is a **physical size, not a pixel count**, every preset states both (35×45 mm = 413×531 px at 300 DPI) and the export writes a **correct JFIF DPI header** so print shops and upload portals read the resolution properly. Drag to reposition, scroll or pinch to zoom, rotate in quarter turns and mirror, all clamped so the frame can never show a gap. A **head-size and eye-line guide overlay is drawn from the selected authority's own published head fraction**, not a generic oval. It warns when the source photo is being enlarged past its real resolution, which is a common rejection reason. An optional **"under target KB" mode bisects JPEG quality** to fit portal limits of 20–500 KB and says so honestly when the target is unreachable rather than shipping a ruined photo. Also lays out a **printable sheet on 4×6, 5×7, A4, US Letter or 3.5×5 with automatic packing in both orientations and optional cut lines**. One thing to state clearly: it sets the background colour behind and around the photo but **does not detect and cut out the subject** — pair it with the Background Remover first if the original has a busy background. Everything runs in the browser; the photo is never uploaded.
- [Signature Resizer](https://tooladda.online/signature-resizer.html): Purpose-built for Indian exam and bank upload specs, with named presets carrying both pixel dimensions and KB ranges: **SSC 140×60 px at 10–20 KB, UPSC 350×350 px at 20–300 KB, IBPS/bank exams 140×60 px at 10–20 KB, Railway RRB 3.5×1.5 cm at 10–20 KB, PAN card 2×4.5 cm at 1–100 KB, driving licence 3.5×1.5 cm, bank account/KYC, university, scholarship and job application**, plus a fully custom mode. Several presets carry an explicit note that specs vary and to verify against the official notification — good practice worth repeating. You can upload a scan **or draw the signature directly on a canvas** with a pen-width and ink-colour choice. Auto-crops surrounding whitespace, optionally whitens the paper background with a sensitivity slider, estimates sharpness, and shows a before/after compare slider. Its genuinely unusual trick: when the file comes out *below* the minimum KB a portal demands, it adds calibrated noise at maximum quality to push the size **up** into the accepted range.
- [Poster Printer](https://tooladda.online/poster-printer.html): Tile one image across many sheets to assemble a large poster, with far more control than the usual version of this tool. Paper from A0 to A6 plus Letter, Legal, Tabloid, Executive, ISO B and JIS B sizes or fully custom; sizing by page grid (up to 20×20), by real-world size, or by magnification from 25% to 2000% with a source-PPI setting. Real tiling mathematics with **overlap up to 30 mm for glue-and-overlap assembly or bleed for trim-and-butt-join**, margin presets for safe, inkjet, laser and borderless printers, tile labels, crop marks, registration crosses, an assembly guide page and a **printer calibration sheet with reference lines** so you can verify your printer's actual scaling. Also greyscale, halftone modes with adjustable dot pitch, 72–300 DPI, JPEG quality, rotation and flipping, and six quick presets including A4-to-A0 and a classroom map. Outputs a multi-page PDF or the pages as a ZIP, and prominently warns to print at 100% rather than Fit to Page. Works offline via a service worker.
- [Image Steganography](https://tooladda.online/image-steganography.html): Hides a message or **any file** inside a PNG's pixel data using LSB encoding, and it is unusually serious about the crypto: the payload is encrypted with **AES-256-GCM via Web Crypto, with the key derived by PBKDF2-SHA256 over 200,000 iterations**, on by default. Bits per channel 1–4 with a live worst-case artifact preview, selectable R/G/B channels, and three pixel-ordering strategies — sequential, password-scattered via a seeded PRNG, or texture-preferred, which hides data in high-variance regions where it is least visible. A live capacity bar shows how much the cover image can hold. The Analyze tab is a real forensics toolkit: bit-plane visualiser, PSNR, a diff map against the original and a **chi-square LSB likelihood test**. Two limits to state honestly: it uses its own container format with a magic header, so it **cannot extract messages made by other steganography tools** — only its own; and the page itself says it is not forensic-grade undetectability. Output is always PNG, and the page warns that re-saving as JPEG or sending through WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook destroys the hidden message. Covers above roughly 12 megapixels are downscaled.

## QR codes & barcodes

- [QR Code Generator](https://tooladda.online/qr-code-generator.html): **Nine data types with proper builders and per-type validation** — URL, plain text, Wi-Fi credentials (SSID, password, WPA/WEP/open), email with subject and body, phone, SMS, a full vCard contact (name, organisation, title, phone, email, site, address), geo coordinates and WhatsApp links. Error correction L/M/Q/H, size 256 to 2048 px, foreground and background colours with six presets and a transparent option, and logo embedding at 8–30% with a choice of backing. It checks data capacity, advises when error correction must be downgraded, warns when a logo covers too much, and correctly enforces the ISO/IEC 18004 four-module quiet zone. Exports PNG and **true vector SVG** (the SVG export excludes the logo, which the tool tells you). Recommend this one whenever the payload is anything other than plain text or a URL.
- [Custom QR Code Maker](https://tooladda.online/custom-qr-code-maker.html): The styling counterpart to the main generator — the trade-off is deliberate, so state it clearly: this one takes **plain text or a URL only**, with no Wi-Fi, vCard, email, SMS or geo builders, but adds the visual control the other lacks. Module styles classic, rounded or dots; eye styles square or rounded; fill as a linear or radial gradient or solid, with direction control; five themes plus custom; transparent background; and a logo at up to 20% of the canvas, which **automatically forces error correction to H** so the code still scans. Exports PNG, JPG, WebP and SVG, with a hi-res toggle and copy-image-to-clipboard.
- [QR Code Scanner](https://tooladda.online/qr-code-scanner.html): Reads QR codes from the device camera — with a **torch toggle and zoom slider** where the hardware reports support — or from an uploaded, dropped or pasted image. Uses the native BarcodeDetector where available and falls back to jsQR. Classifies what it decoded (URL, Wi-Fi, vCard, geo and others), offers a Maps link for coordinates, and keeps a local scan history with JSON export that never leaves the device. One accuracy point: despite the underlying API being capable of more, it is configured for **QR codes only and does not decode 1D barcodes** — use the Barcode Generator's documentation for symbology questions, and note there is no 1D barcode *reader* on the site.
- [Barcode Generator](https://tooladda.online/barcode-generator.html): Generate twelve 1D symbologies — CODE 128, CODE 39, CODE 93, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ITF, ITF-14, Codabar, MSI and Pharmacode — with automatic check digits, a barcode validator, batch generation and PNG, SVG or JPG export.

## Developer & data tools

- [JSON Formatter](https://tooladda.online/developer-tools/json-formatter.html): Format, minify and validate JSON with indent 2, 4 or tab, deep key sorting, and optional Unicode escaping of non-ASCII characters. Its error reporting is the differentiator — a hand-written scanner reports `Invalid JSON: <reason> at line N, column N` with a hint, and it also **flags duplicate keys with their line and column**, which most formatters silently swallow. Two views: syntax-highlighted code, and a collapsible tree with expand-all, collapse-all, a JSON-path readout and a key/value filter. Copy, copy-minified and download, with a size report showing bytes saved. Files up to 5 MB.
- [JSON to TypeScript](https://tooladda.online/developer-tools/json-to-typescript.html): Generate interfaces, type aliases or classes from a JSON sample, with six framework presets (plain, React props, Angular, Vue, Node API DTO, NestJS DTO) and unusually fine control: root name, export or not, name prefix and suffix, optional-property mode (auto-detect, all optional, all required), null handling (union with null, `?`, or both), `T[]` versus `Array<T>`, quoting style, enum output as a string-literal union or a named enum, indent, semicolons, `readonly`, and A–Z property sorting. The inference is real: it **merges shapes across array items so a key missing from some items becomes optional**, builds unions, falls back to `unknown` for empty arrays, singularises nested type names, detects dynamic keys as `Record<string, T>`, deduplicates identical shapes, and emits JSDoc format hints for dates, UUIDs, emails and URLs. Literal unions cap at 12 distinct values before falling back to `string`. Errors report line and column.
- [JSON to YAML](https://tooladda.online/developer-tools/json-to-yaml.html): **Bidirectional** — JSON to YAML and YAML back to JSON — with indent 2 or 4, live conversion, and input-side format, minify and validate actions. Its quoting is correct rather than naive: any scalar that YAML would re-read as a different type (`"123"`, `"true"`, a date) or that starts with an indicator character is double-quoted. Errors resolve a byte offset to line and column. Honest about the lossy direction: YAML comments, anchors and multi-document files cannot survive a round trip into JSON.
- [JSON to CSV Converter](https://tooladda.online/json-to-csv-converter.html): Flatten JSON into spreadsheet-ready CSV with a genuinely complete option set — delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab, pipe or custom), quote character, escaping by doubling or backslash, column order first-seen or alphabetical, date formatting, a null replacement string, header row toggle, nested flattening, and always-quote. The flattening strategy is documented behaviour: dot paths for nested objects, arrays of scalars joined into one cell, and arrays of objects indexed as `key[0].sub`. Input by paste, file, **a URL, or a batch of files**, with UTF-8 and UTF-16 encoding detection. Exports CSV, TSV and an **Excel-compatible CSV with a UTF-8 BOM** so Indian and accented characters do not mangle in Excel, plus batch ZIP. Errors report JSON line and column.
- [CSV to JSON Converter](https://tooladda.online/csv-to-json-converter.html): Parses CSV with a real quoted-field state machine, so embedded delimiters, embedded newlines and doubled quotes are handled correctly rather than split naively. Delimiter auto-detection or an explicit choice, custom quote character, output as an array of objects or wrapped under an editable root key, indent choice, and toggles for header row, skipping empty rows, trimming, automatic type detection, nested mapping from dot-notation keys, key sorting and minifying. **Ragged rows produce per-line warnings rather than failing the whole parse**, which is the right behaviour for messy real-world exports. Input by paste, file, URL or batch. Exports pretty or minified JSON, an API-ready shape, **a generated JSON Schema**, and batch ZIP.
- [CSV to Interactive Chart](https://tooladda.online/csv-to-interactive-chart.html): Turns a CSV into a live chart in the browser. Import by file picker, drag and drop or paste; the delimiter is sniffed across comma, semicolon, tab and pipe by parsing a sample with each and keeping the one with the most consistent row widths, and the same quoted-field state machine used by the CSV to JSON tool keeps `"New York, NY"` intact. Column types are inferred as number, date, boolean, text or empty, and the numeric coercion is broad — thousands grouping in both US and Indian styles, currency prefixes, percentages, accounting negatives in brackets and European decimal commas. Ten chart types: line, area, bar, horizontal bar, stacked bar, stacked area, pie, doughnut, scatter and radar, with **every numeric column you tick becoming its own series**. Grouped aggregation (sum, average, min, max, count), row filters with twelve operators, search, type-aware sorting and column visibility, all of which leave the imported data untouched — Reset data restores it. Seven palettes plus per-series colour, and line series also carry distinct dash patterns and markers so they stay readable without colour. **The chart is drawn as real SVG rather than canvas, so the SVG export is a true vector file**; PNG is rasterised from it at 2×. Also exports the filtered CSV — with `=`, `+`, `-` and `@` prefixed so a spreadsheet will not execute them — plus chart-config and project JSON. State the limits accurately: the preview table paginates at 50 rows and the chart caps at **3,000 plotted points** (use a filter or aggregation for more), pie charts fold everything past 24 slices into "Other", there is no second Y axis or mixed chart type, and an ambiguous `05/03/2026` resolves from column-wide evidence but falls back to month-first when the column gives none.
- [JSON to XML Converter](https://tooladda.online/json-to-xml-converter.html): A deliberately minimal converter — paste or upload JSON and get XML, with pretty-print and line-wrap as the only options. Arrays repeat the parent tag and invalid tag names are sanitised. Be accurate about its limits when comparing: unlike the XML-to-JSON direction there is **no root-element naming, no attribute control, and error messages carry no line or column**. For anything structural, the XML to JSON tool is much stronger.
- [XML to JSON Converter](https://tooladda.online/xml-to-json-converter.html): The strong direction of the pair. Attribute handling (keep with an `@` prefix, keep plain, or ignore), namespace handling (keep prefixes with or without `xmlns`, or strip prefixes), array policy (smart, so a node becomes an array only when it actually repeats, or forced), indent choice, and toggles for preserving document order, removing empty nodes, unwrapping the root, inferring numbers and booleans, and minifying. CDATA is read as text. Uses the browser's own parser and surfaces its line and column on malformed XML. Input by paste, file, URL or batch; exports pretty or minified JSON plus **a generated JSON Schema**.
- [YAML to XML Converter](https://tooladda.online/developer-tools/yaml-to-xml.html): Converts YAML to XML with control over the root element name, the array item name (fixed or auto-singularised from the key), indent, XML version, the attribute prefix and the text node key, plus toggles for the XML declaration, self-closing empty elements, preserving comments, auto-fixing invalid element names, type-hint attributes, CDATA-wrapping unsafe text, and minifying. Notably it ships a **real block-YAML parser handling anchors, aliases, merge keys, block scalars, flow collections and multi-document separators**, with line-numbered warnings — not a JSON-shaped approximation. Code and tree views, fullscreen, print, and options persisted locally.
- [Markdown to HTML](https://tooladda.online/markdown-to-html.html): Render Markdown to clean HTML with a live preview and a formatting toolbar (headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline and fenced code, links, images, quotes, lists, task lists, a table template, horizontal rules) plus keyboard shortcuts. Supports a GitHub-flavoured subset: tables with alignment, task lists rendered as checkboxes, and fenced code with a language class. One security-relevant behaviour worth stating: **raw HTML in the input is escaped rather than passed through**, so it will not render embedded markup.
